generator_metadata.summary: A zero-background grid contains one to three true rectangle-corner colors and one to three deliberately nonqualifying colors.  In first-appearance order, a color with exactly four cells at exactly the corners of its bbox fills that bbox into a fresh output; all other colors disappear.

11. Finite checks do not prove universal uniqueness. Owner qualification/acceptance and training admission remain pending/false.

previous_catalog_record.summary: 0-bg grid (h~5-7, w~8-10) with 1-2 distinct colors, each having EXACTLY 4 cells placed at the 4 CORNERS of a rectangle that spans ≥3 rows AND ≥4 cols. Rule: for each non-bg color in the input, find all its cells. Compute bbox. If the cells are EXACTLY 4 AND they sit at the 4 bbox corners → fill the ENTIRE bbox (every cell in the rect) with that color. Else skip. Output: fresh grid with all qualifying rectangles filled.

scope: Accepted generator repair; finite reviewer evidence, no new maintainer execution

sequential_dependency.intermediate: The completed Stage-A grid together with the first qualifying color supplies the visible color read at each two-point trigger endpoint.
sequential_dependency.step_a: Stage A fills every exact four-corner rectangle into a fresh zero grid in first-appearance order; later qualifying rectangles overwrite earlier overlap cells.
sequential_dependency.step_b: Stage B visits every exactly-two-cell color and fills its bounding box iff exactly one endpoint is still painted with the first qualifying color in the completed Stage-A grid.
sequential_dependency.why_b_depends_on_a: Reversing only Stage A changes which qualifier remains visible in the overlap. That changes an endpoint equality test consumed by Stage B, so at least one bridge decision and the protected-Racket final output change.

This is reviewer-ready only; owner admission remains pending.
